documents.markdownContent: # Welcome to CloudManagementPortal Documentation [**CloudManagementPortal**] portal offers a simple and intuitive web-based user interface, [**CloudManagementPortal **](https://localhost/CloudManagementPortal-overview.html#compute) allows you to - **Manage to compute resources** - Easily access and manage your virtual instances, Load Balancer, and Kubernetes. - You can **create an isolated network, VPC, VPN Gateway, Security groups, IP Manager, and many more.** - **CloudManagementPortal Marketplace** lets users **launch their favorite applications in pre-built format.** **** For **Datacenters | Enterprises | Telecom and Cloud Service** Providers. [**CloudManagementPortal**](https://localhost/) is a complete self-service intuitive [**Cloud Management Portal**](https://localhost/) with extensive features leveraging **Apache CloudStack®** with state of art years of expertise. ## Getting Started with CloudManagementPortal The **CloudManagementPortal ** **account sign-up page** allows you to create **a new CloudManagementPortal account** if you don't already have one. **CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management portal** allows you to access and manages your Cloud resources through a simple and intuitive web-based user interface. - **You can create an account on CloudManagementPortal by following the instructions below.** - Click on the option **create an account.** - The Account creation page that appears on the screen. - Fill out the form with the following information: **Email, Country & Code, Mobile Number, and Password.** - Click on the **Register** Button. - CloudManagementPortal sent a Welcome Email to the registered email address. - To **activate** your **CloudManagementPortal account**, click the **Activate and Setup your Account** button in the welcome email. - Enter the **necessary** details. - Click **Next** button. - Enter your Address details here. - And click the **Register** button. - Now the account is created successfully. - Enter your **email address** and **password** and click Login to explore **CloudManagementPortal **. - Now you can explore the **CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal**. ## How to Login into CloudManagementPortal - To Access the **CloudManagementPortal cloud management portal,** type the URL in your browser and press Enter. - Usually, the default URL type will be **https://yourdomainname/login** - Once you access the URL, it will prompt you for email account and password. - Provide your corresponding credentials and click on Login button. - **The CloudManagementPortal cloud management portal** will allow you to login once your login credentials are validated. ## How to Recover CloudManagementPortal Account Password You can retrieve your account if you forget your password with CloudManagementPortal . - Access your **CloudManagementPortal ** URL and click on the **forgotten password.** - Provide the **email address** that you used to create your account and click on the **Send-Email button.** - You will **receive a password reset link to your specified e-mail account.** - Once you click the link, **a new password prompt will appear**. Enter the new password, then press the **"Submit"** button. - The password for the account has been successfully reset. ---------------------------------------- **About CloudManagementPortal** **[CloudManagementPortal] is a complete self-service intuitive [Cloud Management Portal](https://localhost/) with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.**
documents.htmlContent:
Welcome to CloudManagementPortal Documentation

CloudManagementPortal portal offers a simple and intuitive web-based user interface, CloudManagementPortal allows you to

  • Manage to compute resources - Easily access and manage your virtual instances, Load Balancer, and Kubernetes.
  • You can create an isolated network, VPC, VPN Gateway, Security groups, IP Manager, and many more.
  • CloudManagementPortal Marketplace lets users launch their favorite applications in pre-built format.

For Datacenters | Enterprises | Telecom and Cloud Service Providers.

CloudManagementPortal is a complete self-service intuitive Cloud Management Portal with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.

Getting Started with CloudManagementPortal

The CloudManagementPortal account sign-up page allows you to create a new CloudManagementPortal account if you don't already have one. CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management portal allows you to access and manages your Cloud resources through a simple and intuitive web-based user interface.

  • You can create an account on CloudManagementPortal by following the instructions below.
  • Click on the option create an account.
  • The Account creation page that appears on the screen.
  • Fill out the form with the following information: Email, Country & Code, Mobile Number, and Password.
  • Click on the Register Button.
  • CloudManagementPortal sent a Welcome Email to the registered email address.
  • To activate your CloudManagementPortal account, click the Activate and Setup your Account button in the welcome email.
  • Enter the necessary details.
  • Click Next button.
  • Enter your Address details here.
  • And click the Register button.
  • Now the account is created successfully.
  • Enter your email address and password and click Login to explore CloudManagementPortal .
  • Now you can explore the CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal.

How to Login into CloudManagementPortal

  • To Access the CloudManagementPortal cloud management portal, type the URL in your browser and press Enter.

  • Usually, the default URL type will be https://yourdomainname/login

  • Once you access the URL, it will prompt you for email account and password.

  • Provide your corresponding credentials and click on Login button.

  • The CloudManagementPortal cloud management portal will allow you to login once your login credentials are validated.

How to Recover CloudManagementPortal Account Password

You can retrieve your account if you forget your password with CloudManagementPortal .

  • Access your CloudManagementPortal URL and click on the forgotten password.
  • Provide the email address that you used to create your account and click on the Send-Email button.
  • You will receive a password reset link to your specified e-mail account.
  • Once you click the link, a new password prompt will appear. Enter the new password, then press the "Submit" button.
  • The password for the account has been successfully reset.

About CloudManagementPortal

CloudManagementPortal is a complete self-service intuitive Cloud Management Portal with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.

documents.name: Setup Profile
documents.markdownContent: # **Setup Profile** ## Setting up user profile in CloudManagementPortal **CloudManagementPortal **'s Profile feature allows users to change their password and set up payment settings for their convenience. In addition, users can view their credits, promocodes. The Profile feature in [**CloudManagementPortal **](https://localhost/) provides a comprehensive view of a user's account. - Once you enter into the **CloudManagementPortal** portal, you will see the **My Profile option**, where you can update your information and upload images. - **User credit limit** **(a limit that the admin allocates to the user to use the resource)** - in this option, the user can view their admin-allocated credit limit. - Once every **changes got completed**, click the **Save Changes** button. ## Change password for User Account in CloudManagementPortal Portal - To **change your account password**, click on the **Change Password option** located under My Profile. - **Password change** menu apperas on the screen. - To change your account password, click on the **Change Password** option placed under My Profile. - Now Change Password menu appears on the screen. - **Enter the Old Password** and then **enter the New Password** and confirm it. - Then, Click on the Update button. - Now the **New Password has been updated successfully**. ## Choose your Payment Method in User Account - To **Select your payment**, click on the **Payment setting option** placed under the Change Password option. - **Payment settings** menu apperas on the screen. - Select the **required payment gateways** - It is possible to integrate the **user's own country's payment gateway** into the **CloudManagementPortal CloudStack Billing Portal**, but this should be communicated to **CloudManagementPortal Admin** beforehand. :::info **The CloudManagementPortal CloudStack Billing Portal can be customised to accept payments through the user's home country's payment gateway, however this must first be approved by CloudManagementPortal Admin.** ::: ## Credits & Promocode for User in CloudManagementPortal - Under the **Payment setting option**, click on **Credits & Promo codes** to check your credit limits and offers. - Now the Credits & Promo code option appears on the screen. - Total Credit Limit will display the number of credits available for the user. - Under the Used Credit Limit, the user can view their used credit limit. - Balance Available Credit Limit will display the available credit limits. ## API Access Settings in CloudManagementPortal - Under the **Credit & Promocode**, click on **Request API Access option** to access API setting. - Now **API Access** option appears on the screen. - **CloudManagementPortal API** allows you to **manage** your **Instances** and **other resources** programmatically using **conventional HTTP request**. - **CloudManagementPortal's API** allows you to perform any action you can perform through the Control Panel (except creating personal access tokens). ## Notification Settings in CloudManagementPortal - Under the **Manage API Access**, click on **Notification Settings** option to set notification alerts. - Now **Notification Settings** option appears on the screen. - **Maintenance and outage notification** - To receive notifications about outages and maintenance, the user can enable the Outage and maintenance notification option. - **Invoice prefrence** - When the invoice reminder option is enabled, the user will receive a notification about the bill payment three days before the end of the month. - **Payments Overdue** - By enabling the Payment Overdue option, users can receive notifications regarding overdue payments. ## The process of removing an account from the CloudManagementPortal - Under the **Notification settings**, click on **Access Delete Request** option to delete account from the portal. - Now Account delete request screen appears. - Kindly follow the procedure to **delete your account** from **CloudManagementPortal.** --- **About CloudManagementPortal** **[CloudManagementPortal] is a complete self-service intuitive [Cloud Management Portal](https://localhost/) with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.**

documents.name: What's New
documents.markdownContent: # **What's New** In the provided below document, **[CloudManagementPortal ](https://localhost/) users can explore the most recent release in CloudManagementPortal .** ## CloudManagementPortal's Native Helpdesk In the dynamic landscape of the **public cloud service industry**, customer support plays a pivotal role in nurturing a **strong customer-provider relationship**. Acknowledging the significance of a robust helpdesk, **CloudManagementPortal ** has introduced its own integrated helpdesk, empowering cloud tenants to seamlessly communicate with their cloud providers through the user portal. The **CloudManagementPortal helpdesk acts as a bridge, connecting tenants** cloud requirements with the expertise of cloud admins, who are dedicated to understanding and delivering effective solutions promptly and efficiently. Through the helpdesk, tenants can effortlessly raise support issues with the cloud provider and even attach relevant documents and screenshots to expedite problem resolution. Moreover, tenants can stay updated with email notifications when the support team responds to their requests. Taking self-help to the next level, tenants can also leverage the Knowledgebase and FAQs to resolve common issues independently before seeking further assistance from the customer support team. This approach enables tenants to address basic problems on their own and reach out to support only when necessary, fostering a more streamlined support process. With **CloudManagementPortal's Integrated Helpdesk**, the **public cloud service experience** becomes more **user-friendly and customer-oriented, leading to enhanced satisfaction and efficient problem-solving.** **Features of CloudManagementPortal Native Helpdesk:** - Add support Agents and assign roles - Track response time, resolution time and support agents performance - Generate monthly reports to analyze the service health. - Email notifications for support team and tenants - Supports attachments in different format with the support request - Escalate the support requests internally ## Configure customized Sliders in CloudManagementPortal User panel login page. Below is a guide to **setting up customized sliders on CloudManagementPortal login page.** - Using the credentials, **log in to the admin panel** - An option called **Configuration** can be found at the left side of the panel. Click on it to view the drop-down menu. - From the drop down select on the **General** option. - **General configurations** screens appears. - Click on the **Sliders option.** - The Slider option appears on the screen. Click on the **Add Slider** option on the right side of the panel. - **Page Type** - Select the Page Type :::info Note: As per the current release user can configure customized slide only on the login page. ::: - **Name** - Specify a name in the name box. - **Description** - Specify a description on the description box. - **Interval** - Set the interval in milliseconds (i.e., how many seconds the slide should move). - Attach the sIides and logo as per your requirement within the specified dimension mentioned. - Finally, Click on Save button. - Another slide can be added using the same format. The new slide will appear below the existing slide. :::success **Now the custom slides has been updated successfully.** ::: ## Integrate Social Media Backlinks on the User Panel Footer. Below is a guide to **setting up Social Media Backlinks on the User Panel.** - Using the credentials, log in to the admin panel - An option called Configuration can be found at the left side of the panel. Click on it to view the drop-down menu. - From the drop down select on the **General** option. - From the general option click on the Organization Details option. - **Organization Details** screens appears - On the **social media category** the administrator can configure their social media backlinks which may appears on the footer of the user panel of the portal. - Finally, Click on the **update button** - Social media links have now been configured successfully and can be verified from the user panel. ## Grouping Templates in CloudManagementPortal Below is a guide to Grouping Templates in CloudManagementPortal . - Using the credentials, log in to the admin panel - An option called **Service** can be found at the left side of the panel. Click on it to view the drop-down menu. - From the drop down click on the **Offering Category** option. - From the Offering Category option user can able to see a **filter option. - Click on the dropdown icon to view the offering.** - From dropdown select **VM Grouping option** - VM Grouping screen appears. - At right side of the panel admin can able to see a option called **Add category**. Click on it to create a new category. **Create category screen appears** - **Name** - Specify a name for the category. - **Type** - Select the type as VM Grouping. and select on which type the category offering should be created either in OS or marketplace. select as per the requirement, for the demonstration let select OS type. - Upload the icon for the offerings you are creating as per the mentioned dimension. - **Notes** - Specify a notes in the notes column. - Finally, Click **Add** button. - Now the offering has been created successfully. - On the right side of the panel there is a icon called **Template Grouping Configuration.** - Click on it to add OS flavors into the offering. - Select the OS flavors as per the requirement and click Update button. - Now the Template grouping has been added successfully. - Login to user panel to view **the template grouping** - Now the VM Grouping has been added successfully. ## Sub domain support in CloudManagementPortal Welcome to sub domain configuration guide. This guide is designed to assist admin in configuring their subdomains for the user panel. ### Enabling subdomain option to user panel - Login into the admin portal using the login credentials - Admin panel dashboard appears on the screen. - At left side of the panel the user can be able to see an option called **Configuration option**, click on it to view the dropdown. - From the dropdown, click on the **general** option and select **feature configuration** from the list. - After clicking the **feature configuration** at the right side of the panel, the user can see an option for **quick search**. What's New

In the provided below document, CloudManagementPortal users can explore the most recent release in CloudManagementPortal .

CloudManagementPortal's Native Helpdesk

In the dynamic landscape of the public cloud service industry, customer support plays a pivotal role in nurturing a strong customer-provider relationship. Acknowledging the significance of a robust helpdesk, CloudManagementPortal has introduced its own integrated helpdesk, empowering cloud tenants to seamlessly communicate with their cloud providers through the user portal.

The CloudManagementPortal helpdesk acts as a bridge, connecting tenants cloud requirements with the expertise of cloud admins, who are dedicated to understanding and delivering effective solutions promptly and efficiently.

Through the helpdesk, tenants can effortlessly raise support issues with the cloud provider and even attach relevant documents and screenshots to expedite problem resolution. Moreover, tenants can stay updated with email notifications when the support team responds to their requests.

Taking self-help to the next level, tenants can also leverage the Knowledgebase and FAQs to resolve common issues independently before seeking further assistance from the customer support team. This approach enables tenants to address basic problems on their own and reach out to support only when necessary, fostering a more streamlined support process.

With CloudManagementPortal's Integrated Helpdesk, the public cloud service experience becomes more user-friendly and customer-oriented, leading to enhanced satisfaction and efficient problem-solving.

Features of CloudManagementPortal Native Helpdesk:

  • Add support Agents and assign roles
  • Track response time, resolution time and support agents performance
  • Generate monthly reports to analyze the service health.
  • Email notifications for support team and tenants
  • Supports attachments in different format with the support request
  • Escalate the support requests internally

Additionally, you can also use the [CloudManagementPortal API](https://www.CloudManagementPortal/api). This will enable you to programmatically perform various actions on your instances. You can use them standalone or as part of larger, cloud-based infrastructures.   • We can able to take VM snapshots from the instance details page. Detailed information about VM snapshots are under snapshots section.

Recover VM

  • All the virtual machines which are created in CloudManagementPortal will have four stages. They are:

Creating, Running, Stop, Delete & Expunge

  • Creating - When you create a new instance it will be in creating state.

  • Running - Once your VM has been successfully created, it will be in Running state.

  • Stop - When the VM is stopped state, it will move to stop state.

  • Delete - When you delete a VM without Expunge option has been enabled it will be moved to delete state. Later you can recover the VM using the Recover VM option.

  • Expunge - The VM will transition to this level once it has been totally removed from the infrastructure.

  • Recover VM option only available if the VM status is in Destroyed state.

  • To recover a VM from the destroy state, click on Recover VM option.

  • Click OK to recover the VM from the destroyed state.

  • After few seconds, the VM state will be changed from destroyed to stopped state.
  • Now your VM has been successfully recovered.

Attach ISO

  • If you need to reinstall your virtual machine using ISO, then you can use this option.
  • Once the ISO has been attached successfully, When you reboot the machine, it will automatically boot from the selected ISO.

:::info Note: Make sure that you have backup your virtual machine data before proceeding this option. :::

Reinstall VM in CloudManagementPortal

CloudManagementPortal's instance can be reinstalled by following the procedures below.

  • Step 1 - Click on the Compute option from the side menu of the portal and select Instance.
  • Step 2 - Click on the Instance so that you can view a summary page of the particular instance.
  • Step3 - There you can view the Reinstall icon at right side of the panel, Click on it.
  • Now the Reinstall option appears on the screen.

:::info Note: Make sure that you have backup your virtual machine data before proceeding this option. This option will lead you to data loss. :::

  • Select Instance - In this step, the user must select the OS image that will be created after the reinstallation is finished.
  • Enter the VM name - Here the user needs to enter the name of the instance to install.
  • Finally click OK button.
  • Now the instance has been reinstalled successfully.

Accessing Console in CloudManagementPortal

Using Accessing Console you can able to access the instance through webbrowser.

Below is the following steps for Accessing console for the instance.

  • Step 1 - Click on the Compute option from the side menu of the portal and select Instance.
  • Step 2 - Click on the Instance so that you can view a summary page of the particular instance.
  • Step3 - There you can view the Console icon at right side of the panel, Click on it.
  • Once you click on the Console icon it will opens a new window.
  • Here, the user enters their instance username and password and clicks the Enter key.
  • Now the instance has been logged in.

Destroy VM in CloudManagementPortal

  • To delete an instance of CloudManagementPortal , follow the steps below.

  • Step 1 - Click on the Compute option from the side menu of the portal and select Instance.

  • Now the instance page appears on the screen.
  • Make sure the instance is in the stopped stage before selecting it.
  • Click on the Instance so that you can view a summary page of the particular instance.
  • Click on the Summary option from the menu.
  • A delete option can be found on the panel's right side. Just click it.
  • Now the Destroy VM option appears on the screen.

Step 1 - On the first step the user wants expunge the all associated resources.

Step2 - On the second step the user wants to confirm to delete the instance by entering the name of the VM.

  • Finally click on Destroy button.
  • Now the instance has been deleted successfully.

Instance Resize

CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal offers you flexible way to migrate your instance plan from one plan to another using simple GUI Interface.

  • Resizing an instance in CloudManagementPortal is simple as following these steps

:::info Before resizing the instance, ensure that the instance has been stopped. :::

  • Click on the instance.
  • Click on the resize option to resize the instance.
  • By selecting the option, you can see the size of the current instance.
  • Depending on your needs, you can upgrade or downgrade the size of the instance from the following plans.
  • Click the RESIZE button after selecting the plan..
  • Now the VM has been resized successfully..

Savings Plans in CloudManagementPortal

Savings Plans in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal are a flexible pricing model that offer low prices on resource usage, in exchange for a commitment to a consistent amount of usage (measured in ₹ /hour) for long term.

:::info

  • Before enabling a saving plan ensure the instance is on stopped stage. :::

The user can enable saving plans in CloudManagementPortal in two ways they are,

  • Enable the plan directly by clicking on the instance, which may automatically generate the instance information process.
  • Second method, Enabling the saving plan using the savings plan option from the side menu option.

Enable the saving plan directly by clicking on the instance

  • Method 1
  • Click on the instance.
  • Select Resize from the option.
  • When you scroll down on the panel, you will see an option called Purchase Saving plan.
  • On clicking the Purchase Saving Plan button, the page for Purchase Saving Plan is appear on the screen.
  • Here you can select the offering as per the requirement.

  • Reserved offering type - There are two types of reserved offering they are STANDARD and CONVERTABLE.

    1. STANDARD OFFERING - Users who select the standard offering cannot upgrade or downgrade the offering; they can only maintain the same offering they configured initially.

    2. CONVERTABLE OFFERING - If users select the convertible offering, they can upgrade or downgrade the offering at any time.

RI Plan name

  1. Select the RI plan (i.e. yearly or monthly coverage).
  • Finally Click on the SAVE PLAN option.
  • Now the Reserved offering is successfully configured.

Configure saving plan offering using the configuring saving plan option

  • Method 2

  • Now we will configure saving plan offering using the second method as configuring saving plan option.

  • The billing option can be found on the left side of the panel.

  • Click on it to view the drop-down menu.

  • From the drop-up select the Savings plan.

  • Saving Plan screen appears on the screen.

 

  • Active plan - Here you can see how many Reserved plans are in active.
  • Savings - Using the reserved instance policy, you will be able to see how much amount has been saved by offering saving plan.
  • Plans expire this month - In this section, you can see the plans that going to expire this month.
  • Current Active Plans - This section shows the Current Active Plan and necessary details.
  • At the bottom of the page you can able to see an option called Purchase Saving Plan.
  • Click on it to Purchase a Saving plan for your resource.
  • Purchase a Saving plan screen appears.
  • Here you can choose the offering as per the requirement.

  • Reserved offering type - There are two types of reserved offering they are STANDARD and CONVERTABLE.

    1. STANDARD OFFERING - Users who select the standard offering cannot upgrade or downgrade the offering; they can only maintain the same offering they configured initially.

    2. CONVERTABLE OFFERING - If users select the convertible offering, they can upgrade or downgrade the offering at any time.

RI Plan name

  1. Select the RI plan (i.e. yearly or monthly coverage).

Instance

  1. In this case, the user wants to select the VM on which a saving plan will be configured.
  • Finally Click on the SAVE PLAN option.
  • Now the Reserved offering is successfully configured.

Storage and Snapshot

  • This section will provide you the functionality to add additional storage to your virtual instance. Also, there are few enhanced features for your virtual storage such as Resize, Volume snapshot, Recurring Snapshot & Create Template.

Network & Firewall

  • One of the most essential part for your virtual instance is Network and Firewall. This section provide you various features to add additional functionality & security for your virtual instances.

  • In addition to this, Load balancer feature will be included to all the source NAT IP under each isolated network.

  • Please refer the Networking section for more information.

Monitoring agent in CloudManagementPortal

  • CloudManagementPortal Portal will provide you the detailed monitoring feature to monitor your virtual resources like CPU Usage, Memory Consumption, I/O, Network, Disk Usage, Process etc.

  • Please refer monitoring section for more information.

Access & Security

  • CloudManagementPortal will provide additional security features to your virtual machines such as SSH key pair. You can able to add or upload existing SSH key pair under this section.

VM Scheduler in CloudManagementPortal

  • VM Scheduling is process of start or stop your virtual machines automatically at certain date and time. Using CloudManagementPortal you can achieve this.

With CloudManagementPortal's VM scheduler, you can start and stop instances automatically. You can manage instances more efficiently by automating the process with a VM scheduler. You can set up instance schedules for both on-off workloads.

For example, use VM scheduler to only run VM instances during working hours.

The Vm Scheduler Guide for CloudManagementPortal is provided below.

  • Compute option can be found on the left side of the panel click on it view the pop up.
  • From the pop up click on the instance option.
  • Click on the particular instance.
  • Now the summary of the particular instance appears on the screen.
  • At the right side of the panel you can see a option for Vm scheduler, Click on it.
  • Click Create on the button.
  • VM Scheduler screen appears on the screen.
  • Scheduler name - Give a name for the scheduler.
  • VM Action - Here select the action that you are going to set (i.e start or, stop).
  • Week days - Here select the specific days that Instance should perform.
  • Time zone - Mention a specific time zone to perform the scheduler process on the specific time.
  • Finally click create button.
  • Now the VM scheduler has been created successfully.

Notes

  • Notes - In this option the user can take notes.

About CloudManagementPortal

CloudManagementPortal is a complete self-service intuitive Cloud Management Portal with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.

documents.markdownContent:
# Introduction

**CloudPortal** provides block-level storage volumes to use with our virtual instances. These volumes can be attached to your virtual instance which makes its data and file system available for your nodes. If your instance is running on Linux or windows, then you can mount this volume and format the storage based on your file system.

**CloudPortal** block storage can be useful when your storage needs get increased more than your computing demands, Since these block storage volumes are directly connected to your virtual instance.

## Storage And Snapshot in CloudPortal Cloud Management Portal

A storage volume is a virtual disk that provides persistent block storage space for instances in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal Service. :::success

Delting the Volume in CloudManagementPortal

:::success

documents.name: Extend the Root Volume
documents.markdownContent: # Extend the Root Volume ### In this tutorial, we'll show you how to extend **Windows VM's root volume.** - We assume that, You have changed the virtual instance root volume size, for example, **40 GB to 50 GB** while creating the instance. - Once you logged in the server, open run command and type diskmgmt.msc - Your additional space will be show as **unallocated** in the disk management snap-in. - To extend your root volume, right click on c: drive and click on extend volume. - A new wizard will be open and click Next to continue. - Specify the amount of space that you willing to expand and click Next button. - Click finish to complete the wizard. - Now you can able to see your root volume with new disk size.
documents.htmlContent:
Extend the Root Volume

In this tutorial, we'll show you how to extend Windows VM's root volume.

  • We assume that, You have changed the virtual instance root volume size, for example, 40 GB to 50 GB while creating the instance.
  • Once you logged in the server, open run command and type diskmgmt.msc
  • Your additional space will be show as unallocated in the disk management snap-in.
  • To extend your root volume, right click on c: drive and click on extend volume.
  • A new wizard will be open and click Next to continue.
  • Specify the amount of space that you willing to expand and click Next button.
  • Click finish to complete the wizard.
  • Now you can able to see your root volume with new disk size.

documents.name: Attach Data Volume
documents.markdownContent: # Attach Data Volume ### Steps to attach a data volume in windows VM - Let's assume that you have already created a VM and volume has been attached to your windows instance. - Login into your windows instance and right click on the windows button and select **disk management.** - While access the disk management snap-in, it automatically detects your attached disk and prompt to initialize the disk. Click **OK** to continue. - Currently, your attached disk will be in **unallocated** state. - Right click on the disk and select **New Simple Volume**. - New wizard will popup, click **Next** to continue. - Specify the volume size, by default it takes **total disk space.** Then click **Next.** - Assign a **drive to your disk** and click **Next.** - Specify a filesystem for your disk. documents.markdownContent: # Extend the Data Volume ### In this tutorial, we'll show you how to extend **Windows VM's data volume.** - Let's assume that you have already created a VM and volume has been attached to your windows instance. :::info Note: Make sure that you virtual instance should be in **stopped state** before performing the below operation. ::: - Also, For ex, you have resize your data disk by adding additional **10 GB through CloudManagementPortal portal.** - Start your virtual machine. - Once you logged into your virtual machine, Open run window and type **diskmgmt.msc** - You are able to see the **additional disk space as an unallocated state.** - Right click on the data disk and click on **extend volume.** - A new wizard will be open and click **Next** to continue. - Specify the amount of space that you willing to expand and click **Next** button. - Click **finish** to complete the wizard. - Now you can able to see your data volume with new disk size.

# Introduction

**CloudManagementPortal volume snapshot** is a point-in-time copy of the data stored on a storage volume or disk. It's a mechanism used to create a backup or a copy of the data in case of a disaster or data loss.

A volume snapshot captures the state of the data at the time the snapshot is taken, which allows users to restore data to that particular point in time. This is useful in scenarios where you want to revert to an earlier state of the data or recover deleted data.

# Introduction

**CloudManagementPortal** VM (Virtual Machine) snapshot is a point-in-time copy of a virtual machine's disk file and memory state. It allows users to capture the state of a virtual machine at a particular moment, which can be useful for a variety of purposes, such as backup, disaster recovery, testing, and troubleshooting.

When a VM snapshot is taken, a copy of the virtual machine's disk file and memory state is created, which is saved as a separate file. This file can be used to restore the virtual machine to its previous state if needed.

- [Creating VM Snapshot](/help/docs/user-guide/vm-snapshot/creating-vm-snapshot#creating-vm-snapshot-in-CloudManagementPortal-) 
- [How to Revertback VM Snapshot](/help/docs/user-guide/vm-snapshot/revertback-vm-snapshot#how-to-revertback-vm-snapshot-in-CloudManagementPortal-)

documents.name: Auto Scaling Deployment
documents.markdownContent: ### Add Autoscaling feature to the instance in CloudManagementPortal - Click on the **Virtual Resources** dropdown button below the dashboard icon, Which is available in the top left corner. from the dropdown, Click on **Autoscaling**, to create a Autoscaling policy. - **Choose a Load balancer** - Identify the load balancer for which the Auto Scale policy should be created. - **OS Template** - Select the OS template. - **Compute Offer** - Choose the Compute offer as per the requirement. - **SSH Keypair** - Select the SSH Keypair. - Click **Next** button. - On the second step complete the configuration process for the Autoscale policy. - **Scaling Policy** - Select the Scaling policy as per the requirement. - **Warmup interval** - When creating a new capacity provider or updating an existing one, you can specify a custom instance warm-up time, and you can set instance warm-up time in seconds. - And click the **NEXT** button. - **In this section, you can review your policy in detail.** - If you want to edit the previous page you can edit using the Edit option which is placed above the page. - Click **Review and launch** button to launch the policy. - documents.name: Create New SSH key
documents.markdownContent: # Create New SSH Key An **SSH key** is an **access credential** in the SSH protocol. documents.markdownContent:
# What is Affinity Group


### Affinity group On CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal.

- **A positive rule tries to run the virtual machines together on a single host; a negative affinity rule tries to run the virtual machines apart on separate hosts**.

- Affinity group is a feature that allows users to group the resources together so that we can work together more efficiently. Affinity groups can be used to ensure that resources are located in the same data center or region, which can improve network latency and reduce data transfer costs.

- When you create an affinity group, you can specify a geographic location for the group, and then add resources to the group. The resources that are added to the group will be located in the same data center or region as the affinity group. This can be useful for applications that require low latency or high availability, as resources that are located closer together can communicate more quickly and reliably.

-----------------------------------------------------

documents.name: Basic Network
documents.markdownContent: ## Network Administrator in CloudManagementPortal [**CloudManagementPortal**](https://localhost/) provides private networks, traffic filtering, and load balancing to help you protect and control the traffic of your applications. [**CloudManagementPortal**](https://localhost/) provides private networks, traffic filtering, and load balancing to help you protect and control the traffic of your applications. - There are two types of networks available in **CloudManagementPortal **: **L2 network** and **Isolated network**. ### L2 Network in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal - Click on the **Network** dropdown below the virtual resources icon, available in the top left corner. From the dropdown, click on **Basic Network** to create a new network. - The **Basic Network** screen appears. - On the right side of the panel, the user can see an option called **ADD NETWORK**, click on it. - Then, once you click on the Add Network button, select the type of network required according to your needs. :::info **The following document shows the flow of L2 Network.** ::: - **Name**: Specify a **name** for the network. - **Network Offering** - Select the **Network Offering**. - **Attach Network to Instance**: The user can **attach the network** to their **required instance** using this option. - Finally, click on the **Create** button. - Now the **L2 Network** has been successfully created. ### Creating an Isolated Network in CloudManagementPortal **An isolated network can only be accessed** through virtual machines from a single account. - Click on the **Network** dropdown below the virtual resources icon, available in the top left corner. From the dropdown, click on **Basic Network** to create a new network. - The **Basic Network** screen appears. - On the right side of the panel, the user can see an option called **ADD NETWORK**, click on it. - Once you click on the **Add Network** button, select the option **Isolated Network** to create an **isolated network**. :::info **The following document shows the flow of Isolated Network.** ::: - **Name**: Specify a **name** for the network. - **Network Offering** - Select the **Network Offering**. - **Attach Network to Instance**: The user can **attach the network** to their **required instance** using this option. - Finally, click on the **Create** button. :::success - Now the **Isolated Network** has been successfully created. ::: ## Adding Network to Instance in CloudManagementPortal - Click on the **Virtual Resources** dropdown below the panel icon, available in the top left corner. From the dropdown, click on the **Instance** option. - The instance screen appears. - Click on the specific instance. - Now the instance summary page appears. Select the **Network and Firewall** option in the summary. - The Network and Firewall option appears. - On the right side of the panel, click on **Add Network to VM**. - Select the Network and click on the **Add** button. **IMG** - Now the virtual machine is successfully connected to the network. ## Adding Security Groups in CloudManagementPortal - Click on the **Network** dropdown below the calculation icon, available in the top left corner. From the dropdown, click on the **Security Groups** option. - The **Security Group** option appears on the screen. - On the right side of the panel, the user can see an option called **Add**. Click on it to **create new security groups**. - **Name**: Specify a **name** for the security group being created. - **Description** - Provide brief notes about the security group. - **Status**: Specify the IP version. - Finally, click on the **Add** button. :::success **- Now the security group has been created successfully.** ::: ### What is Network Address Translation (NAT)? - **NAT** stands for **Network Address Translation**. - It will translate a set of IP addresses to another set of IP addresses. - In other words, as explained by Wikipedia, "**Network Address Translation is a method of mapping an IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets while they are in transit across a traffic routing device**." - In **CloudManagementPortal **, there are two types of NAT available. They are: **Source NAT** and **Static NAT**. - **Source NAT** - It will be used as shared NAT, meaning, using this Source NAT IP, we will be able to access multiple virtual machines. - **Static NAT** - It will be the dedicated NAT. In other words, this NAT IP will be connected to a single virtual machine. It's like a one-to-one communication. ## Configuring Port Forwarding - **Port Forwarding** allows a computer over the Internet to connect to a specific computer (or) service within a private network. - A port number will have an IP address, and based on the port number, it will determine what the purpose is. - Click on the **Network** dropdown below the virtual resources icon, available in the top left corner. From the dropdown, click on **Basic Network**, **to configure port forwarding**. - The **Basic Network** screen appears. - Click on the **network** you want to configure port forwarding for. - The network details screen appears. Select the **Public IP** section on the details screen. - Click on the **NAT Source** option. - IP address screen opens. - Before setting up port forwarding, the user must set up the firewall. - To configure the Firewall, click on the **Firewall** option and set it up. - Once the firewall is configured, go to the **Port Forwarding** option. - Click on **Add VM**. - Configure the required port and select the protocol. - Finally, click on **Add VM and Configure**. - Now the port forwarding has been configured successfully. ## Creating an Egress Rule in CloudManagementPortal - The **egress rule** will be used to allow your virtual instance to access the external network, i.e., the **Internet**. - Click on the **specific security group where the egress rule should be created**. - **Now the egress rule creation menu appears.** - The user can see an option called **Add Rule** on the right side of the panel. - Click on that. - Select the **protocol** according to your preference. - Specify the **starting and ending port number.** - Finally, click on the **Add Rule** button. :::success - The egress rule has now been successfully created. ::: ## IP Manager Overview in CloudManagementPortal **An IP address in CloudManagementPortal ** is a static **publicly accessible IP address** that you can assign to an **instance** and later **reassign** to **another instance**. To create a high availability infrastructure, you can implement a failover mechanism using reserved IP addresses. ## Obtaining a New Public IP Address - Click on the **Network** dropdown below the calculation icon, available in the top left corner. From the dropdown, click on the **IP Manager** option. - The **IP Manager** screen appears. - Click on the option **Acquire new public IP**. - *Choose Your Network* - To acquire a public IP address, choose the network. :::note *Load balancing and port forwarding functions can be enabled by disabling Static NAT while acquiring a new public IP address.* ::: :::note *Load balancing and port forwarding functions can be disabled by enabling Static NAT while acquiring a new public IP address.* ::: - To confirm the acquisition of the new IP address, click on the checkbox. :::note *- The administrator charges a fee for acquiring a new IP address.* ::: - Finally, click on the *Acquire* button. - Now the *IP address* has been successfully created. ## Releasing Public IP Address :::note *Load balancing and port forwarding functions can be disabled by enabling Static NAT while acquiring a new public IP address.* ::: - To release a public IP, click on the *release icon* available in the *Action menu*. - You will receive a confirmation notification in the portal once you click on it. - To release the IP address, click on Accept. - Now your *IP* has been *successfully removed*. ## Virtual Private Cloud *INTRODUCTION* VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is a network feature in the cloud control panel that allows users to create isolated and logically defined private cloud environments within a public cloud infrastructure. VPC enables users to have full control over their network topology and allows them to configure a private network space with multiple levels of virtual machines, routers, firewalls, and load balancers. *VPC FEATURES* - Isolated Network Environment: VPC allows users to create an isolated network environment with its own private IP address space. This isolation provides increased security and separation from other VPCs and the public cloud. - Multiple Levels: Within a VPC, users can create multiple levels or subnets to efficiently organize their network infrastructure. Each level can have its own set of virtual machines and network services such as routers, load balancers, and firewalls. - Virtual Router: The VPC uses a virtual router to provide essential routing capabilities between different levels within the VPC and also between the VPC and the external network (public cloud or Internet). The virtual router handles network traffic and ensures that packets are correctly forwarded to their destination. - Network ACLs and Security Groups: VPC allows users to define Network Access Control Lists (ACLs) and security groups to control incoming and outgoing network traffic to and from the virtual machines in the VPC. This helps improve security and access control to VPC resources. - VPN Connectivity: VPC supports the creation of Virtual Private Network (VPN) connections, allowing users to establish secure communication between their on-premises infrastructure and the VPC in the public cloud. This feature enables hybrid cloud scenarios and facilitates secure data transfer. - Load Balancing: Users can configure load balancers within the VPC to distribute incoming traffic among multiple virtual machines at a level. This ensures high availability and scalability for applications running within the VPC. - Network Offering: VPC offers multiple network offerings that define the specifications and capabilities of the VPC, such as the number of subnets, IP address ranges, and supported services. Users can select the appropriate network offering based on their requirements. - Elastic IP Addresses: VPC provides Elastic IP (EIP) addresses that can be associated with virtual machines to allow them to have a static and public IP address. This enables the virtual machines to be accessed from the Internet without changing their IP addresses. *STEPS TO CREATE A VIRTUAL PRIVATE CLOUD* - Log in to your control panel. - Go to Network and click on VPC. - Then click on Add VPC. - Provide the name, description, and specify the IP address range for the VPC in CIDR notation (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16). This range should not overlap with other networks in your CloudManagementPortal environment. Also, choose the appropriate VPC offering that defines the specifications and capabilities of the VPC. Then click on the Add button. ![VPC Configuration](https://localhost/apidocs/resources/VPC2/34a2b109586b4fcbaebba1b17bb810f8.jpg) - VPC created successfully. *ADD YOUR VPC LEVEL NETWORK* - After creating your VPC network, click on the configure button. - Then click on create network. - Specify the name of your level (e.g., "DMZ", "Application", etc.) - Select the appropriate ACL to allow or deny access to your network. - Then provide the gateway, netmask, select the network offering for your level, and click on the Add button. - Your new level network has been created successfully. *ADDING VIRTUAL MACHINES* - To create a new virtual machine, click on the virtual machines link. - Then click on Add instance. - *[Steps to create an instance](/docs/virtualresources/Instance#quick-deploy-in-CloudManagementPortal-)* - When creating the VM, make sure to have selected your VPC level from the network list. *CONFIGURING VPC TO VPC VPN IN THECLOUD* - To explain VPC to VPC VPN, refer to the image below for demonstration. *VPN Gateway*: The VPN gateway is the term used for the local VPN endpoint. This is simply enabled on the NAT source IP address of the VPC virtual router and allows the local VR to accept incoming VPN connections. *VPN Client Gateway*: The VPN client gateway is the remote endpoint that we target when setting up the VPN connection. When setting these up, we must specify all details for this VPN connection. - Name: user-friendly name for the gateway - Gateway: public IP address of the remote VPC virtual router. - CIDR List: this is a list of CIDR networks that can be reached at the remote end of the tunnel. Multiple CIDR ranges can be specified, separated by commas. - Pre-Shared IPsec Key: this is effectively the VPN password phrase used when negotiating the VPN connection and as such should follow standard password best practices in a production environment. - IKE/ESP encryption details for the VPN tunnels. *VPN Connection* The VPN connection is the pairing from the originating (or local) VPN gateway to the remote VPN client gateway. This is configured in one of two modes: - Active: the connection that initiates the VPN tunnel, typically from the VPC hosting the virtual machines consuming resources in the remote VPC. - Passive: this connection waits for the opposite VPC VR to initiate the connection and is typically in the VPC hosting the resources to be consumed. Note that for both connections, resources at both ends must be reachable via the CIDR list configured for the VPN client gateway. *STEPS TO CREATE A VPN GATEWAY* - Log in to the cloud control panel. - Then click on Network and select VPN Gateway. - Then click on the ADD VPN button. - In this example, we assume that the virtual machines from VPC1 Level 1 and 2 will consume resources in VPC2. Note that in this case, we only configure the name, public gateway, CIDR list, and pre-shared IPsec key; all other fields are left as default. - Repeat this step for the client gateway in VPC2: *Enabling Site-to-Site VPN* - Log in to your cloud control panel. - Then click on the VPC menu. - Click on the corresponding VPC from the list. - Then click on configure. - Click on the Site-to-Site VPN list menu. - Click Accept to confirm the creation. - Once the Site-to-Site VPN is enabled, click on the VPN Connection tab. Click on the Add button. - Then select the VPN Gateway from the dropdown list and click Accept. - Repeat this step for the passive connection from VPC2 to VPC1, but for this one, check the "passive" checkbox. - Once both VPN connections are configured, refresh the screen and ensure that the VPN Connection status is "connected". - If the VPN connection does not appear automatically, simply go back to the active connection (from VPC1 to VPC2) and click the "Reset" button. ## Overview of Load Balancer in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal A *load balancer* can be deployed as *software or hardware* on a device that *distributes client connections* among a set of servers. A load balancer acts as a "**reverse proxy**" to represent the application servers to the client through a virtual IP address (VIP). This technology is known as *Server Load Balancing (SLB)*. SLB is designed for groups of application servers within a single site or local area network (LAN). ### Add a load balancer to an instance in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal - Click on the *Network* dropdown button below the *Compute icon*, which is available in the top-left corner. In the dropdown menu, click on *Load Balancer* to create a new Load Balancer. - The *Load Balancer* screen appears. - On the right side of the panel, you can see an option called *Create Load Balancer*, click on it. - The option to *Add Load Balancer* appears on the screen. - As a first step, enter a *name and description* for the load balancer you create. *Network and IP Address* - Here you select the network and IP address for the Load Balancer. - *Create Forwarding Policy and Algorithm* - *Policy Name*: provide a policy name. - Select the protocol and assign a port number for both the load balancer and the instance. *Choose Algorithm and Sticky Sessions* - Choose your Load Balancer algorithm for traffic distribution. - Select the sticky session as per requirement. *Attach Instance* - Attach the policy to the required instance and click the *Save Policy* button below. - Now the *Load Balancer Policy* has been created successfully. - Once the policy is created successfully, click on the *Create Load Balancer* button available below. - The *load balancer is successfully configured on the instance.* - Now you can see the created policy in the Load Balancer panel. -------------------------------------------------- --- About The Cloud CloudManagementPortal is an intuitive and full-featured self-service cloud management portal with extensive capabilities leveraging Apache CloudStack® and years of cutting-edge technology experience.

An IP address in CloudManagementPortal is a static publicly accessible IP address that you can assign to an instance and later reassign to another instance. To create a high availability infrastructure, you can implement a failover mechanism using reserved IP addresses.

Obtaining a New Public IP Address

  • Click on the Network dropdown below the calculation icon, available in the top left corner. From the dropdown, click on the IP Manager option.

  • The IP Manager screen appears.

  • Click on the option Acquire new public IP.

  • Choose Your Network - To acquire a public IP address, choose the network.

:::note Load balancing and port forwarding functions can be enabled by disabling Static NAT while acquiring a new public IP address. :::

:::note Load balancing and port forwarding functions can be disabled by enabling Static NAT while acquiring a new public IP address. :::

  • To confirm the acquisition of the new IP address, click on the checkbox.

:::note - The administrator charges a fee for acquiring a new IP address. :::

  • Finally, click on the Acquire button.

  • Now the IP address has been successfully created.

Releasing Public IP Address

:::note Load balancing and port forwarding functions can be disabled by enabling Static NAT while acquiring a new public IP address. :::

  • To release a public IP, click on the release icon available in the Action menu.

  • You will receive a confirmation notification in the portal once you click on it.

  • To release the IP address, click on Accept.

  • Now your IP has been successfully removed.

Virtual Private Cloud

INTRODUCTION

VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is a network feature in the cloud control panel that allows users to create isolated and logically defined private cloud environments within a public cloud infrastructure. VPC enables users to have full control over their network topology and allows them to configure a private network space with multiple levels of virtual machines, routers, firewalls, and load balancers.

VPC FEATURES

  • Isolated Network Environment: VPC allows users to create an isolated network environment with its own private IP address space. This isolation provides increased security and separation from other VPCs and the public cloud.

  • Multiple Levels: Within a VPC, users can create multiple levels or subnets to efficiently organize their network infrastructure. Each level can have its own set of virtual machines and network services such as routers, load balancers, and firewalls.

  • Virtual Router: The VPC uses a virtual router to provide essential routing capabilities between different levels within the VPC and also between the VPC and the external network (public cloud or Internet). The virtual router handles network traffic and ensures that packets are correctly forwarded to their destination.

  • Network ACLs and Security Groups: VPC allows users to define Network Access Control Lists (ACLs) and security groups to control incoming and outgoing network traffic to and from the virtual machines in the VPC. This helps improve security and access control to VPC resources.

  • VPN Connectivity: VPC supports the creation of Virtual Private Network (VPN) connections, allowing users to establish secure communication between their on-premises infrastructure and the VPC in the public cloud. This feature enables hybrid cloud scenarios and facilitates secure data transfer.

  • Load Balancing: Users can configure load balancers within the VPC to distribute incoming traffic among multiple virtual machines at a level. This ensures high availability and scalability for applications running within the VPC.

  • Network Offering: VPC offers multiple network offerings that define the specifications and capabilities of the VPC, such as the number of subnets, IP address ranges, and supported services. Users can select the appropriate network offering based on their requirements.

  • Elastic IP Addresses: VPC provides Elastic IP (EIP) addresses that can be associated with virtual machines to allow them to have a static and public IP address. This enables the virtual machines to be accessed from the Internet without changing their IP addresses.

STEPS TO CREATE A VIRTUAL PRIVATE CLOUD

  • Log in to your control panel.
  • Go to Network and click on VPC.
- Then click on Add VPC.

  • Provide the name, description, and specify the IP address range for the VPC in CIDR notation (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16). This range should not overlap with other networks in your CloudManagementPortal environment. Also, choose the appropriate VPC offering that defines the specifications and capabilities of the VPC. Then click on the Add button.

  • VPC created successfully.

ADD YOUR VPC LEVEL NETWORK

  • After creating your VPC network, click on the configure button.
  • Then click on create network.
  • Specify the name of your level (e.g., "DMZ", "Application", etc.)
  • Select the appropriate ACL to allow or deny access to your network.
  • Then provide the gateway, netmask, select the network offering for your level, and click on the Add button.
  • Your new level network has been created successfully.

ADDING VIRTUAL MACHINES

  • To create a new virtual machine, click on the virtual machines link.
  • Then click on Add instance.
  • Steps to create an instance
- When creating the VM, make sure to have selected your VPC level from the network list.

CONFIGURING VPC TO VPC VPN IN THECLOUD

  • To explain VPC to VPC VPN, refer to the image below for demonstration.

VPN Gateway: The VPN gateway is the term used for the local VPN endpoint. This is simply enabled on the NAT source IP address of the VPC virtual router and allows the local VR to accept incoming VPN connections.

VPN Client Gateway: The VPN client gateway is the remote endpoint that we target when setting up the VPN connection. When setting these up, we must specify all details for this VPN connection.

  • Name: user-friendly name for the gateway
  • Gateway: public IP address of the remote VPC virtual router.
  • CIDR List: this is a list of CIDR networks that can be reached at the remote end of the tunnel. Multiple CIDR ranges can be specified, separated by commas.
  • Pre-Shared IPsec Key: this is effectively the VPN password phrase used when negotiating the VPN connection and as such should follow standard password best practices in a production environment.
  • IKE/ESP encryption details for the VPN tunnels.

VPN Connection

The VPN connection is the pairing from the originating (or local) VPN gateway to the remote VPN client gateway. This is configured in one of two modes:

  • Active: the connection that initiates the VPN tunnel, typically from the VPC hosting the virtual machines consuming resources in the remote VPC.
  • Passive: this connection waits for the opposite VPC VR to initiate the connection and is typically in the VPC hosting the resources to be consumed.

Note that for both connections, resources at both ends must be reachable via the CIDR list configured for the VPN client gateway.

STEPS TO CREATE A VPN GATEWAY

  • Log in to the cloud control panel.

  • Then click on Network and select VPN Gateway.

  • Then click on the ADD VPN button.

  • In this example, we assume that the virtual machines from VPC1 Level 1 and 2 will consume resources in VPC2. Note that in this case, we only configure the name, public gateway, CIDR list, and pre-shared IPsec key; all other fields are left as default.

  • Repeat this step for the client gateway in VPC2:

Enabling Site-to-Site VPN

  • Log in to your cloud control panel.

  • Then click on the VPC menu.

  • Click on the corresponding VPC from the list.

  • Then click on configure.

  • Click on the Site-to-Site VPN list menu.

  • Click Accept to confirm the creation.

  • Once the Site-to-Site VPN is enabled, click on the VPN Connection tab. Click on the Add button.

  • Then select the VPN Gateway from the dropdown list and click Accept.

  • Repeat this step for the passive connection from VPC2 to VPC1, but for this one, check the "passive" checkbox.

  • Once both VPN connections are configured, refresh the screen and ensure that the VPN Connection status is "connected".

  • If the VPN connection does not appear automatically, simply go back to the active connection (from VPC1 to VPC2) and click the "Reset" button.

Overview of Load Balancer in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal

A load balancer can be deployed as software or hardware on a device that distributes client connections among a set of servers. A load balancer acts as a "reverse proxy" to represent the application servers to the client through a virtual IP address (VIP). This technology is known as Server Load Balancing (SLB). SLB is designed for groups of application servers within a single site or local area network (LAN).

Add a load balancer to an instance in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal

  • Click on the Network dropdown button below the Compute icon, which is available in the top-left corner. In the dropdown menu, click on Load Balancer to create a new Load Balancer.

  • The Load Balancer screen appears.

  • On the right side of the panel, you can see an option called Create Load Balancer, click on it.

  • The option to Add Load Balancer appears on the screen.

  • As a first step, enter a name and description for the load balancer you create.

Network and IP Address

  • Here you select the network and IP address for the Load Balancer.

  • Create Forwarding Policy and Algorithm

  • Policy Name: provide a policy name.

  • Select the protocol and assign a port number for both the load balancer and the instance.

Choose Algorithm and Sticky Sessions

  • Choose your Load Balancer algorithm for traffic distribution.

  • Select the sticky session as per requirement.

Attach Instance

  • Attach the policy to the required instance and click the Save Policy button below.

  • Now the Load Balancer Policy has been created successfully.

  • Once the policy is created successfully, click on the Create Load Balancer button available below.

  • The load balancer is successfully configured on the instance.

  • Now you can see the created policy in the Load Balancer panel.

documents.markdownContent: # Security Group Firewall - The purpose of **Security groups in CloudManagementPortal ** is to isolate traffic to virtual machines. - Security groups are groups of virtual machines that filter their traffic based on ingress and egress rules. - According to these rules, network traffic is filtered according to the IP address trying to communicate with the virtual machine. - The use of security groups is especially useful in zones using basic networking, since all guest VMs have their own network. - The KVM hypervisor is the only hypervisor that supports security groups in advanced zones. ### Add security group in CloudManagementPortal - Click on the **Network** dropdown button below the compute icon, Which is available in the top left corner. from the dropdown, Click on **Security Groups** option. - Security groups screen appears - At the right side of the panel the user can able to see a button called **Add**, click on it. - Enter the name and give a short description - And select the status. - Finally, Click on **Add** button. - Now the security group has been created successfully. - In the **Action** section we can **edit,manage,and delete** the **security group.** ----------------------------------------------------- **About CloudManagementPortal** **[CloudManagementPortal] is a complete self-service intuitive [Cloud Management Portal](https://localhost/) with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.**

documents.markdownContent: # Saving Plans ## Savings Plan in CloudManagementPortal Cloud Management Portal Savings Plans in [**CloudManagementPortal**](https://localhost/) are a flexible pricing model that offer low prices on resource usage, in exchange for a commitment to a consistent amount of usage (measured in ₹ /hour) for long term. - Click on the **Billing** dropdown button below the **Monitoring** icon, Which is available in the top left corner. from the dropdown, Click on **Saving plan**. - **Saving plan** screen appears. - **Active plan** - Here you can see how many **Reserved plans are in active.** - **savings** - **Saving option** allows users to see how much money they have saved in comparison to a normal plan. - **Plans expire this month** - In this section, you can see the plans that **going to expire on this month.** - **Current Active Plans** - In this section shows the **Current Active Plan and necessary details.** - At the bottom of the page you can able to see an option called **Purchase Saving Plan.** - Click on it to **Purchase a Saving plan**. - Select the **Offering plan** as per the requirement. - **Reserved Offering** - In CloudManagementPortal there are two types offering avilable they are **Standard**, and **Convertable**. - **Standard offering** - In the **standard offering**, users can only use the policy in the standard format and cannot upgrade or downgrade it. - **Convertable offering** - Using **Convertable offering**, the user can upgrade the reserved instance policy at any time. - Select the offering as per the requirement. - **RI plan name** - Here select the reserve instance policy duration. - **Instance** - **Choose the instance** to **which the policy should be attached.** - Finally click on **Save Plan**. - Now the reserved instance policy has been configured successfully. ----------------------------------------------------- **About CloudManagementPortal** **[CloudManagementPortal] is a complete self-service intuitive [Cloud Management Portal](https://localhost/) with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.**

documents.name: Introduction
documents.markdownContent:
# Introduction


In the organization section in **CloudManagementPortal ** user can view the flow of the **user profile, user manager, RBAC, quota limit, maintenance, and my Activity.**

- **User profile**: This refers to the information associated with a user account, such as their Change Password, Payment Settings, Credits & Promo code, Notification settings any other relevant details.
- **User manager**: This refers to the tool or interface used to manage user accounts, including adding new users, modifying existing users, and deleting users.
- **RBAC**: This stands for **Role-Based Access Control**, which is a method of granting different levels of access to resources based on a user's role or job function.
- **Quota limit**: This refers to a limit placed on the amount of resources (such as storage space and bandwidth etc..,) that a user is allowed to consume.
- **My Activity**: This refers to a feature that allows users to view their activity in the **CloudManagementPortal Portal.**


- [User profile](/help/docs/user-guide/organization/User-Profile#setting-up-profile-in-CloudManagementPortal-)
- [User Manager](/help/docs/user-guide/organization/User-Profile#add-user-in-CloudManagementPortal-)
- [RBAC](/help/docs/user-guide/organization/User-Profile#setting-up-role-privileges-in-CloudManagementPortal-)
- [Quota Limit](/help/docs/user-guide/organization/User-Profile#quota-manager-in-CloudManagementPortal-)
- [My Activity](/help/docs/user-guide/organization/User-Profile#my-activity-in-CloudManagementPortal-)

-----------------------------------------------------


**About CloudManagementPortal**

**[CloudManagementPortal] is a complete self-service intuitive [Cloud Management Portal](https://localhost/) with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.**

documents.name: User Profile
documents.markdownContent: # User Profile ## Setting up Profile in CloudManagementPortal - **Company** option can be found on the left side of the portal. - The screen displays a pop-up menu. From the pop uu click on **Profile**. - **My Profile** option appears on the screen. - The user can view or edit their personal information here. - Users can **upload their company logo or profile here.** - Finally,Click on the **Save Changes** button below the portal once the changes have been made. ### Changing login password in CloudManagementPortal - On the left side of the pop-up menu, users can change their password by clicking on the **Change Password** option. - **Old Password** - Enter your Old password. - **New password**- Enter **The new password** in the **new password field.** - Re-Type the **new password in the Confirm password field**. - Finally, Click the **Update** button. - Now the New password has been updated successfully. ### Payment Configuration on CloudManagementPortal - On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the **Payment Configuration** button to configure payment gateways. - Here user can Choose their **payment gateways** for the **payment process.** :::info - CloudManagementPortal is a plug-and-play solution that **supports all kinds of payment gateways.** - All kind of payment gateways can be intregrated with CloudManagementPortal by **API** concept. ::: - By Default CloudManagementPortal has two payment gateways they are **Paypal, and Razorpay.** ### Credits and promocodes in CloudManagementPortal - On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the **Credits and promocodes** button to view the credits and promocode offers. - Here the user can see the **total credit** which was assigned by the **admin.** - In this section, the user can view their **total credit limit**, **how much has been consumed, and the balance available credit limit for the next month.** - Below, Admins can assign users offers and promo codes here so that users can see if they have any. ### Request API Access in CloudManagementPortal - To view the API Documentation, Click On the **Request API Access**. - So that the request will sent to the admin through the email. ### Notification Settings in CloudManagementPortal - On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the **Notification settings** button to set notifications. - The user can enable the **Send Email Maintenance and Outage Notifications button** to receive notifications regarding **maintenance and outages.** - Enable the **Invoice remainder** option, the user will **receive a notification for the invoice.** - Enabling the **Payment overdue** option will allow the user to **receive a notification for the overdue** ### Account Delete Request in CloudManagementPortal . - On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the **Delete Account** button to **Delete Account in CloudManagementPortal .** - We recommend that you to follow these steps before deleting your account. - Account delete screen appears on the screen. - Click on the **Request for account delete**. ** img 888 ** - So here user can able to see the resources which has been attached to the particular account. ## Add User in CloudManagementPortal - **Company** option can be found on the left side of the portal. - The screen displays a pop-up menu. From the pop up click on **user**. - **Add users** page appears on the screen. - To add a user, click the **Add user.** - **Fill all the required information on the menu.** - Finally, click **Add button.** :::success - **Now the new user has been created successfully.** ::: ## Setting up Role Privileges in CloudManagementPortal **CloudManagementPortal Role-based access control (RBAC)** restricts network access based on a person's role within an organization and has become one of the main methods for advanced access control. The roles in RBAC refer to the levels of access that employees have to the network. - Typically there is a **default role which is named domain admin.** - **Company** option can be found on the left side of the portal. - The screen displays a pop-up menu. From the pop up click on **Role Privileges**. - **RBAC** screen appears. - At left side of the panel the user has a option to create new role. - Click on **Create New Role**. - Assign access rights to users so that they can access resources. - Once every process done, click on the **Update** button. :::success - **Now the Role Privelage has set successfully.** ::: ## Quota Manager in CloudManagementPortal - The **Company** option can be found on the left side of the portal. - The screen displays a pop-up menu. To view the Quota, click on the **Quota Limit** option from the menu. - Now Quota Limit page appears on the screen. - The user can see a detailed view of the resources that have been allocated by the administrator. - Users can request an upgrade from their Admin if they need to upgrade any resources. ## My Activity in CloudManagementPortal - The **Company** option can be found on the left side of the portal. - The screen displays a pop-up menu. To view the recent activities, click on the **My Activity** option from the menu. - Here user can be able to see their recent activities. - Here the user can be able to see the Alerts. ----------------------------------------------------- **About CloudManagementPortal** **[CloudManagementPortal] is a complete self-service intuitive [Cloud Management Portal](https://localhost/) with extensive features leveraging Apache CloudStack® with state of art years of expertise.**

Setting up Profile in CloudManagementPortal

  • Company option can be found on the left side of the portal.
  • The screen displays a pop-up menu. From the pop uu click on Profile.

  • The user can view or edit their personal information here.

Changing login password in CloudManagementPortal

  • On the left side of the pop-up menu, users can change their password by clicking on the Change Password option.
  • Old Password - Enter your Old password.

  • Re-Type the new password in the Confirm password field.
  • Finally, Click the Update button.
  • Now the New password has been updated successfully.

Payment Configuration on CloudManagementPortal

  • On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the Payment Configuration button to configure payment gateways.
  • Here user can Choose their payment gateways for the payment process.

:::info

  • CloudManagementPortal is a plug-and-play solution that supports all kinds of payment gateways.

  • All kind of payment gateways can be intregrated with CloudManagementPortal by API concept. :::

  • By Default CloudManagementPortal has two payment gateways they are Paypal, and Razorpay.

Credits and promocodes in CloudManagementPortal

  • On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the Credits and promocodes button to view the credits and promocode offers.

  • Here the user can see the total credit which was assigned by the admin.

  • In this section, the user can view their total credit limit, how much has been consumed, and the balance available credit limit for the next month.
  • Below, Admins can assign users offers and promo codes here so that users can see if they have any.

Request API Access in CloudManagementPortal

  • To view the API Documentation, Click On the Request API Access.
  • So that the request will sent to the admin through the email.

Notification Settings in CloudManagementPortal

  • On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the Notification settings button to set notifications.
  • The user can enable the Send Email Maintenance and Outage Notifications button to receive notifications regarding maintenance and outages.
  • Enable the Invoice remainder option, the user will receive a notification for the invoice.

Account Delete Request in CloudManagementPortal .

  • On the left side of the pop-up menu, Click on the Delete Account button to Delete Account in CloudManagementPortal .
  • We recommend that you to follow these steps before deleting your account.
  • Account delete screen appears on the screen.
  • Click on the Request for account delete.

** img 888 **

Add User in CloudManagementPortal
